exposure: first-trimester serum pregnancy-associated plasma protein-A (PAPP-A) levels
first-trimester serum free beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (b-hCG) levels
cohort: The cohort consisted of 119 pregnancies diagnosed with intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) and a randomly selected subcohort of 383 pregnancies from the same general population.
finding: Lower first-trimester serum PAPP-A levels and b-hCG levels below the 10th percentile were significantly associated with an increased risk of intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR).
